title: SpaceX Plans 2027 Launch of Space-Based AI Computers Co-Designed With Nvidia

tickers.name: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A Common Stock

summary:
SpaceX is partnering with Nvidia to build AI computing centers that will operate in orbit to bypass power constraints on Earth. The aerospace company targets the third quarter of 2027 to begin deploying the hardware, with volumes slated to ramp up in 2028 and 2029, according to CEO Elon Musk. Musk noted that orbital sites provide 30% more solar power than ground-based facilities and that the cost of producing intelligence in space is lower once the cost per ton to orbit is reduced.

Investor Ron Baron expressed support for the move, arguing that the U.S. must increase domestic chip production and electricity generation to compete with China. Baron estimated that China adds approximately 300 gigawatts of power capacity annually compared with 20 gigawatts in the U.S., and that China's total power capacity is roughly three times that of the U.S.

BREAKING: Ron Baron backs Elon Musk to put data centers in space.

“We need more power and Elon’s doing that.”

• Baron says America needs to build more chips at home and generate more electricity. “We need more power. Elon’s doing that.”

• By Baron’s estimate, China has roughly 3× the power capacity of the U.S. and adds about 300 gigawatts a year, compared with 20 in the U.S.

• Baron says Musk is targeting launches in 2027 and 2028 to bring solar-powered data centers into orbit.

• He expects data centers in space to be “significant in 2028” and “huge” a year or two later.
